transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m getting pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be trying to finish a dashboard, and then one Slack notification, or even a song lyric or some random idea for another project, and I just lose the thread of what I was doing. It’s been frustrating.
Have you had times when your mood felt unusually high or wired?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can get excited about things or stay up later than I meant to, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had times where my mood felt unusually high or wired.
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?

Yeah, I think so. Even in elementary school, teachers would write comments that I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions because I’d lose track. I also remember getting in trouble for talking over other kids during group work.

At home, my parents would sit next to me while I did homework because otherwise I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished.
Do these focus problems also cause trouble for you outside of work?

Yeah, it does. It’s not just work. I’ve lost a couple small freelance contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly or missed details, and I missed out on a portfolio competition too.

It’s also affected friends and people I collaborate with. They’ll say they like my ideas, but some of them are hesitant to work with me because they’re not sure I’ll be reliable.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?
Not really, no. I mean, I’ll get random thoughts or worries like anyone, but I don’t think I have thoughts that keep forcing themselves in when I’m trying to ignore them.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
I don’t think so. I worry sometimes if there’s something actually going on, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying a lot for no clear reason.
